If you need a furnace filter or a key cut in Dawson, you won't have to drive to Madison for it after all.

Main Street Hardware, which announced in July that its longtime owners planned to retire, has been sold to a couple from the area who say they will keep it open. The sale is expected to close at the end of October. (This is a demo story; the store and the owners are fictional.)

When a small-town store closes, people lose more than a place to shop. They lose a short trip. A 25-mile drive for a single hinge adds up fast, and some of that spending tends to follow people to the bigger town for good.

The new owners say they plan to keep the current staff of four and the store's hours. They also want to add online ordering with in-store pickup, which they hope will win back some customers who have drifted to big-box stores.

That's a reasonable idea, though not a guarantee. Small hardware stores run on thin margins, and the new owners are taking on inventory and a building that needs a new roof, according to the sale listing.

Still, the store has buyers, and the lights stay on. For a town of about 1,400 people, that counts.
